findings.title: Executor-hosted solve starves the HA loop 97% of the time; the solve's own GIL yields move it 0.75 points
findings.claim: With the production solve on a ThreadPoolExecutor thread (the _await_optimize fallback path), a 1 ms heartbeat on a real event loop sees a longest contiguous GIL hold of 36.9 ms and a starvation share of 0.9737, and removing all eight 2 ms production yields leaves the longest hold at 28.0 ms and moves the share only to 0.9812.
findings.mechanism: The eight sleep(0.002) calls sit BETWEEN L-BFGS-B runs (3 between consecutive multi-start starts, 4 in _lbfgsb_restart, 1 at the DHW/space seam). The maximum heartbeat gap is therefore set by the longest single L-BFGS-B run, which no between-run yield can bound. The 32 ms of yielding is 1.08% of the solve's wall time and buys 0.75 of a percentage point of starvation share.

evidence.unit: fraction of solve wall in heartbeat gaps > 5 ms
evidence.machine: Apple M1 8-core, 8 GB, OpenBLAS, CPython 3.11, 1 BLAS thread
evidence.contention_note: Shared box: D4 (Chromium) and D8 auditing concurrently; load1 5.71 at this measurement, 4.5-8.8 across the session
evidence.tolerance: +/-10% on the two wall figures; the starvation-share ratio is stable to ~0.01 across re-takes

perturbation.change: --perturb no-yields: all production time.sleep calls neutralised for the duration of the solve (the eight yield calls become no-ops, production_yield_total_ms 32.000 -> 0.000)

findings.metric_definition: Longest contiguous GIL hold = max gap between 1 ms heartbeat ticks on a real asyncio loop while optimize() runs on an executor thread; starvation share = fraction of solve wall in gaps > 5 ms.

null_control.note: A known 300 ms of loop-thread work is reported as a longest hold of 301.1 ms and a starvation share of 1.0037, so the instrument reads a known block correctly. A second control, --perturb same-thread (solve on the loop thread), reports 2865.3 ms, i.e. the whole solve.

findings.proposed_fix_scope: Do not try to fix this by adding more between-run yields: the gap is inside an L-BFGS-B run. Either accept it and delete the eight inert yields (they cost 32 ms per solve on the shipped path, where the solve is in another process, and buy 0.75 points on the fallback path), or bound the hold where it is created by capping the per-run iteration budget and restarting, which changes the solver's iterate path and therefore needs the golden drift lane. Any change to the yields is a timing-only edit by construction and moves no plan.

findings.title: Stress gate's simulate-work channel cannot see ThermalModel.simulate_dhw_only
findings.claim: tests/stress.py:SolverWork counts simulate step-equivalents only on ThermalModel.simulate_step and ThermalModel.simulate_trajectory_batch, so the DHW planner's own 24 simulate_dhw_only calls per solve (2304 step-equivalents, 29.6% of all simulated work on the single-zone DHW solve) are counted by neither channel.
findings.mechanism: SolverWork wraps exactly two class attributes. The DHW planner reaches its simulation through a third entry point, ThermalModel.simulate_dhw_only, used by every _dhw_plan_temps call and by _repair_dhw_floor's up-to-48-round loop. A synthetic 2x regression confined to that planner therefore moves neither counted channel, and near a third of the simulated work on the single-zone DHW solve is off a counted seam.

evidence.unit: uncounted share of all simulated step-equivalents
evidence.machine: Apple M1 8-core, 8 GB, OpenBLAS, CPython 3.11, 1 BLAS thread
evidence.contention_note: Shared box with D4 and D8; this metric is an integer count and is contention-immune

findings.instrumented_symbol: heatpump_optimizer.thermal_model:ThermalModel.simulate_dhw_only (uncounted) against ThermalModel.simulate_step and ThermalModel.simulate_trajectory_batch (the two seams tests/stress.py:SolverWork wraps)

perturbation.change: --case two_zone_space: the same solve with dhw=False (no tank volume configured)
perturbation.observed_value: dhw_only_simulate_steps 2304 -> 0 (dhw_only_calls 24 -> 0) while the counted channel stays non-zero at 64512

findings.metric_definition: Uncounted share = simulate_dhw_only step-equivalents / (simulate_dhw_only step-equivalents + step-equivalents on the two seams SolverWork wraps), per full optimize() call.

null_control.note: With the DHW channel off the uncounted count is exactly 0 while the counted channel is 64512, so the harness is measuring the DHW planner and not a constant.

reproduction_steps: for c in single_zone_dhw two_zone_dhw zero_range_pin fuseguard_cap two_zone_space; do PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tools/audit/round6/D9/h1_gradient.py --case $c; done
findings.proposed_fix_scope: Add ThermalModel.simulate_dhw_only to SolverWork's wrapped set, charging each call its schedule length (one step-equivalent per planned step, the same rule the scalar seam uses). One class body and one restore line in tests/stress.py; it changes no count the gate already judges except the DHW planner's, so it needs a baseline capture beside the run rather than a budget re-record. Bounded severity: the DHW planner's CPU share is under its step share, so this is a coverage hole in the instrument, not a wrong plan.
